rounds.text: Taurian MPS Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 110% over three years [E14] and a massive 117% compounded profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E17]. This performance is supported by a robust sector tailwind in Capital Goods [E55, E57] and a consistent ability to generate high returns, with a 3-year median ROE of 31% [E20]. The company is actively reinvesting in its future, as shown by a 233.3% surge in capital work-in-progress [E31], which suggests that the current growth trajectory is being fueled by deliberate capacity expansion. Furthermore, the market appears to be undervaluing these prospects, as the stock trades at an EV/EBITDA of 7.91x, significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 12.25x [E11]. A discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 918, providing a 22.5% margin of safety at the current price [E36, E37]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E26, E27], high debtor days [E46], and a decline in institutional ownership [E33, E34, E35].

Taurian MPS Ltd presents a significant disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, evidenced by a negative cash conversion ratio of -2.31x and a free cash flow of Rs -48 Cr in Mar 2026 [E26, E28]. This liquidity strain is compounded by deteriorating working capital efficiency, as debtor days have ballooned to 181 and total working capital days have surged from 150 to 227 [E46, E47]. Investors should be wary of the valuation, as the stock trades at a P/E of 39.01x against a sector benchmark of 21.96x and a P/B of 6.65x [E2, E6]. Furthermore, institutional confidence appears to be eroding, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping significantly since Sep 2025, resulting in a negative money flow signal [E33, E34, E35]. The company also fails to provide any direct return to shareholders, maintaining a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical sales and profit growth [E14, E16] and maintains a return on equity that exceeds sector benchmarks [E9, E13].

The bear’s focus on negative cash flow ignores the company’s aggressive growth phase, where Capital Work in Progress has surged by 233.3% [E31]. This deliberate reinvestment of capital explains the temporary cash strain as the firm scales operations to capture the current sector tailwind [E55, E57]. While the bear highlights high debtor days [E46], it fails to acknowledge that the company is fundamentally outperforming its sector, with sales growth of 110% and profit growth of 292% over three years [E14, E16]. The valuation premium is justified by this superior performance, as the company’s ROCE of 29.7% and ROE of 26.7% dwarf the sector benchmarks of 13.5% and 11.34% respectively [E9, E12, E13, E60]. Conceded: the company currently has a negative free cash flow of Rs -48 Cr and a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E28]. Furthermore, the bear’s reliance on institutional outflows ignores the fact that the stock is currently trading at an EV/EBITDA of 7.91x, which is significantly cheaper than the sector benchmark of 12.25x [E11]. Finally, the intrinsic value of Rs 918 per share suggests that the market has not yet fully priced in the company's rapid earnings expansion [E36, E38].

The bull dismisses negative cash flows as a mere byproduct of an aggressive growth phase and a 233.3% surge in Capital Work in Progress, but this glosses over severe working capital deterioration where debtor days have blown out to 181 days and total working capital days have ballooned from 150 to 227 days [E31, E46, E47]. Conceded: the company boasts a 3-year sales growth of 110% and profit growth of 292% [E14, E16]. However, this paper growth has completely failed to materialize into actual liquidity, resulting in a disastrous negative free cash flow of Rs -48 Cr, negative operating cash flow of Rs -37 Cr, and a cash conversion ratio of -2.31x [E26, E27, E28]. Furthermore, the bull uses an EV/EBITDA of 7.91x to claim cheapness while ignoring the glaring P/E of 39.01x and P/B of 7.27x, both of which command a massive, unjustifiable premium over sector benchmarks of 21.96x and 2.41x [E6, E7, E11]. The bull’s dismissal of institutional outflows as irrelevant ignores broad-based abandonment, as promoters, foreign institutions, and domestic institutions have all slashed their stakes by 3.93, 3.26, and 5.88 percentage points respectively [E32, E33, E34, E54]. Finally, pointing to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value offers little comfort when the company is flagged for potentially capitalizing interest costs and returning a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting profits [E4, E36, E43, E45].
